take: The ratio is the story here. Hidden Links Society sells about thirty products and is documenting a hundred golf courses, and that is a lopsided way to run a clothing brand — which is the point. The catalogue is good on its own terms: real weight in the brass, an overshirt heavier than it needs to be, headcovers made in Oregon.
But the Public 100 project is what the shop is funding, and the 2% is accounted for rather than implied.
It suits the player who wants the purchase to point at something beyond the purchase. Eighteen pieces run $20 to $82.
story_extra: Hidden Links Society sells thirty products and is documenting a hundred golf courses. That ratio is the most interesting thing about them, and it is the reason they are in here.

On the surface this is another small-batch golf brand doing rope caps and chenille patches. The catalogue is good — the brass has real weight to it, the overshirt is heavier than it needs to be, the headcovers are made in Oregon — but it is not, by itself, unusual. What is unusual is what they are doing alongside it.
